## Purpose

Prompt/agent evaluation tooling — runs real agents against a dataset, scores the output with
deterministic checks and a judge model, and reports whether a prompt edit actually helped.

**It spends money and is invoked deliberately by a developer** (`./eval.sh`), never by CI or
`pytest` (`testpaths=["tests"]` never walks it; its own unit tests live under
`tests/unit/test_grading_*.py`).

## Shape

- [backend/evals/__init__.py](../../backend/evals/__init__.py) — states the module's reason for living outside `tests/`.
- [backend/evals/minimal/workflow.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/workflow.py) — the one place that knows a workflow is a directory
  (`workflows/<id>/{workflow.yaml, rubrics/<stage>.yaml, datasets/<name>.json}`);
  `resolve_config` folds a `configs/*.yaml` config and its dataset into the flat dict every other
  module reads, so `prototype`, `ppt`, or a future workflow need no Python change. Deliberately
  named [workflow.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/workflow.py) (singular) against a sibling `workflows/` directory.
- [backend/evals/minimal/run.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/run.py) — dispatch: one dataset row through `agents.factory`/
  `agents.loader` to a response, optionally seeded from an earlier stored run (`--from`/`--into`,
  avoids re-sampling upstream stages). The only module besides [checks.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/checks.py) that touches the
  agent runtime.
- [backend/evals/minimal/checks.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/checks.py) — free, deterministic checks (no model call); dispatches by
  the workflow-declared `checks:` name (`html_prototype` reuses `app.agents.static_check` /
  `app.agents.render_check` directly) so a check measures exactly what production enforces.
  Never imports [judge.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/judge.py).
- [backend/evals/minimal/judge.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/judge.py) — the only module that spends tokens: scores a response
  against a rubric via a judge model, static structured per-dimension schema, bounded
  rate-limit retry and incomplete-reply retry.
- [backend/evals/minimal/score.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/score.py) — pure aggregation/comparison (`aggregate()`, `compare()`,
  `noise_band()`); zero I/O, no model calls, no imports from the rest of the package.
- [backend/evals/minimal/store.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/store.py) — the one path owner for `.runs/<run_id>/` (config/run/judge/
  score JSON, per-phase logs, artifacts); append-only, superseding a prior write into
  `superseded/` rather than overwriting.
- [backend/evals/minimal/report.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/report.py) — builds the static [report.html](../../backend/evals/minimal/report.py) by reading only stored
  JSON via `store` and [score.aggregate](../../backend/evals/minimal/score.py); never recomputes a number itself.
- [backend/evals/minimal/cli.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/cli.py) — argument parsing and printing only; `all` (the normal entry
  point via `./eval.sh`) dispatches then checks/scores each stage that ran.

## Why this shape

The package is split by responsibility along a strict data-flow boundary — dispatch ([run.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/run.py))
produces raw responses, deterministic checks ([checks.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/checks.py)) and the judge ([judge.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/judge.py)) **score
them independently and never import each other**, [score.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/score.py) aggregates with zero I/O, and
[report.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/report.py)/[cli.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/cli.py) only read what was already computed and stored.

That keeps "what did this run cost/produce" ([store.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/store.py), append-only, nothing ever silently
overwritten) separate from "was it good" ([checks.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/checks.py) + [judge.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/judge.py)) separate from "did it
actually improve" ([score.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/score.py)'s noise-aware `compare()`).

The workflow indirection in [workflow.py](../../backend/evals/minimal/workflow.py) is the reason adding a second evaluated pipeline needs
no Python: everything downstream takes a resolved config dict, never a workflow name.
Deliberately excluded: no CI wiring, no automatic scheduling — a run is always operator-triggered
because it spends real API budget.
